correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and exhaustively reconstructed from the definition. A \(2\)-traceability violation uses two parents and an outside nearest codeword, so three-codeword compatibility is an exact local criterion. The verifier checks all \(41{,}664\) triples, all \(635{,}376\) four-subsets, reruns the literal parent/descendant/nearest-codeword definition on every one of the \(27{,}696\) maxima, and performs a complete target-size-five search with only logically sound incompatible-triple pruning. The natural symmetry generators preserve the definition; their orbit closures are disjoint, remain inside the complete maximum set, and sum to the entire census. The reported stabilizers follow from orbit-stabilizer in the order-\(82{,}944\) group.

value.rationale: The parameter \(q=4\) is the terminal alphabet on the small branch of the exact length-three formula: the maximum equals \(q\) for \(q=2,3,4\), while the larger \(\lfloor(3q-3)/2\rfloor\) branch takes over at \(q=5\). A complete equality classification at this transition is structurally informative: there are seven inequivalent extremal types rather than a unique diagonal construction, and maximum codes can have minimum distance \(1\), \(2\), or \(3\). This is a natural complete extremizer classification with a reproducible exhaustive proof, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of the already known maximum value.
